newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Zaire to resume cobalt shipments this week -- source.
newsitem.headline: Zaire to resume cobalt shipments this week -- source.

text.p: Zaire, thrown into a civil war, expects its next shipment of cobalt to take place this week as production of the metal has resumed, a senior African industry source said.

Referring to the head office of Generale des Carrieres et des Mines (Gecamines), which was shut down earlier this month as the the rebel force took over Lubumbashi, the source said: "Everything was back to normal by Monday (last week)."
"It (the next cobalt shipment) will be next week. The production was stopped only for a few hours," he said in an interview.
Cobalt prices have risen over the past few months as Zaire's rebel force, led by Laurent Kabila, advanced and took control of the country's mineral rich Shaba province.
The source said the rebel forces had caused no damage to the country's mining facilities, adding: "I think Kabila is more market-orientated."
By Friday last week, the only big mining area which was not yet under rebel control was Tshikapa in the southwest of the country, the source said.
Yet the source said Gecamines could survive without production for a long time as its cobalt stocks outside the country totalled several thousand tonnes.
The African industry source said Gecamines' offices in London and Brussels, where financial lines are arranged, were now also in the hands of rebels.

Asked about a denouncement by the Zaire Mobutu government of a $1 billion mining deal between Kabila's rebels and a North American company, the source said: "They have no control of anything. How can they say that?"

The government of President Mobutu Sese Seko said on Thursday the deal between the Canadian company America Mineral Fields Inc with rebels to reactivate mines in Shaba province was invalid and stood revoked.

The industry source said that was one of many projects discussed since last year between foreign companies and the Mobutu government. The Canadian company was not the only one that was now in talks with the rebels, the source said.
